A Bastard's Tale, developed and published by No Pest Productions, is a deliberately unforgiving 2D action game that channels the spirit of early console-era difficulty while layering in directional combat mechanics that demand precision and patience. Rather than leaning on elaborate storytelling or modern progression systems, the game builds its identity around mastery of fundamentals. You control a lone armored warrior armed with a longsword, stepping into a hostile medieval world where survival hinges entirely on reading enemy patterns, choosing the correct attack direction, and timing blocks with care. From the first encounter, it becomes clear that this is not a button-mashing hack-and-slash but a measured, tactical experience disguised within retro aesthetics.

The visual style embraces pixel art reminiscent of 16-bit action titles, with rustic villages, grim farmlands, and fortified strongholds forming the backdrop of its five core stages. Character sprites are simple yet expressive enough to communicate intent, particularly during combat animations where directional attacks and shields are central to the design. The restrained art direction works in the game’s favor, keeping the screen readable during chaotic encounters while reinforcing its old-school identity. Complementing the visuals is a soundtrack rooted in chiptune sensibilities, offering energetic but unobtrusive melodies that echo the era it draws inspiration from. Together, the audiovisual presentation creates a cohesive retro atmosphere without feeling overly derivative.

Combat is unquestionably the heart of the experience. Every encounter demands attention because enemies attack from different angles and require corresponding directional responses. Blocking is not automatic, and offensive strikes must be aimed correctly to break through defenses. This system introduces a layer of strategy uncommon in many side-scrolling action games. Standard foes can overwhelm careless players, while later adversaries introduce variations in speed, shield use, and attack rhythm that force constant adaptation. Boss battles amplify these mechanics, functioning as extended tests of pattern recognition and endurance. Success feels earned rather than granted, and each victory reinforces the satisfaction of gradual improvement.

However, the same mechanics that define its strength also contribute to its polarizing reputation. The difficulty curve is steep, and early deaths are frequent as players adjust to the directional system and timing windows. The game offers little hand-holding, instead expecting experimentation and repetition as the path to mastery. For players who thrive on demanding gameplay loops reminiscent of classic arcade or early console challenges, this structure can be deeply rewarding. For others, especially those accustomed to more forgiving checkpoints or layered progression systems, the rigidity may feel punishing. Hit detection and responsiveness generally serve the design well, though occasional moments of perceived unfairness can break immersion and heighten frustration.

Narrative presence is minimal. There is no elaborate lore exposition, no dialogue-driven character arcs, and no branching storylines. The experience is almost entirely gameplay-focused, with its identity rooted in mechanical challenge rather than narrative depth. While this may disappoint players seeking rich storytelling, it also ensures that the game remains tightly focused. The absence of narrative distractions places every ounce of emphasis on combat performance and player improvement. In this sense, the title functions almost like a distilled combat trial—a compact arena of escalating tests rather than a sprawling adventure.

Despite its relatively short campaign, replayability is supported through modes like New Game Plus and an endless survival-style option that encourages high-score chasing and endurance runs. Achievements provide additional incentive for players who enjoy refining their approach or perfecting stage clears. Because the core mechanics are built around precision, repeated playthroughs often reveal subtle efficiencies and improved reaction timing, reinforcing the idea that mastery is a gradual process. The limited number of stages means the experience does not overstay its welcome, but it also leaves some players wishing for additional environments or enemy variety.

Overall, the game stands as a focused homage to challenging retro action titles, delivering a mechanically driven experience that prioritizes skill over spectacle. It does not attempt to modernize itself with expansive RPG systems or cinematic storytelling, instead doubling down on directional swordplay and methodical pacing. For players who appreciate disciplined combat systems and the satisfaction of conquering difficult encounters through repetition and learning, it offers a concise but intense journey. Those seeking broader variety or narrative depth may find it sparse, but within its chosen framework, it delivers a deliberate and uncompromising test of reflexes and resolve.

It might seem like I'm exaggerating, or meming, but Im being completely honest when I say that this changed the way I see gaming when it comes to anger. When I died right at the end of a stage, I didn't want to rage, just to improve. And learning this lesson has improved my experience with other games, especially fighting games. Play this game, and play it for your own sake.

I think I ripped enough into an obscure, near decade old, indie game but it's a shame because it had a lot of potential that I feel wasn't exactly achieved. "A Bastard's Tale" is a platform game characterised by its retro style and challenging gameplay. Players make their way through a dark and dangerous world, trying to defeat enemies. Success in this game requires accurate timing, reflexes and strategic thinking.

The most distinctive feature of the game is its minimalist visual style. The black-and-white colour palette and simple design give the game a unique aesthetic, while encouraging players to focus on the complex gameplay.

The difficulty level can be high and the game's learning curve can sometimes challenge players. However, these challenges, when achieved, provide great satisfaction and help players hone their skills.

Enemies and traps encountered throughout each level in the game encourage players to take up the challenge. Accurate timing of strikes and quick thinking are required to defeat enemies. This adds a tactical dimension to the game, while at the same time ensuring dynamic and fast-paced gameplay.

However, some players may not prefer its minimalistic visual style and high difficulty level. Also, the game's short length and limited variety of content may be a negative aspect for some players.

Overall, "A Bastard's Tale" is an attractive option for players who enjoy retro platformers. Its minimalist visual style, challenging dungeons, and tactical combat mechanics make it stand out. If you like retro gaming experiences and challenge, this game might be interesting for you.

[quote][b]S U M M A R Y[/b][/quote]

[u][b]A Bastard's Tale[/b][/u] is a 2D side-scrolling action game that has a huge emphasis on blocking, counter-attacking, and spacing, and is more akin to a slow and deliberate fighting game. It has a very steep learning curve where death is an inevitability as you arduously struggle to learn your foes' visual cues and attempt to overcome them one at a time.

Overall, I don't recommend it because it's simply a frustrating experience that doesn't respect your time — learning the enemies' telegraphed attacks is a burden and the bosses are even more exhausting and grueling as you are forced to grind through the levels over and over again just to have a singular chance at facing them.

I also found that it wasn't very satisfying, nor did I experience any real sense of accomplishment, when I did finally defeat a new enemy type for the first time. Instead, I had more of a sense of relief that it was over which was soon dashed and replaced with a sense of dread when I died to the next new enemy type and was faced with the prospect of having to do the entire level all over again just to get back to where I was in order to learn the visual cues of the new enemy.

That aside, the sprites aren't animated very well but some of the backgrounds are surprisingly pleasing to look at, the music is unexpectedly good but forgettable, the story is compelling and very minimalistic in nature so it's left entirely up to your interpretation, and the controls are unintuitive in general.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]A C H I E V E M E N T S[/b][/quote]

The game has 12 achievements which artificially inflate the playtime of the game as you must finish it three times, each time slightly more difficult, and reach a certain number of kills in the endless mode. I recommend avoiding this game altogether unless you're a glutton for punishment or just relish in cruel games.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]R E V I E W[/b][/quote]

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The gameplay employs a unique and novel combat system that revolves around you and your enemies being able to block and attack in three directions: to your left side, above you, and to your right side. As a result, the combat hinges on you reacting to the visual cues telegraphed by your enemy in order to block and then counter-attack during their recovery time or after they've finished their attack pattern. Despite the 2D view, most attacks are well-telegraphed and it is obvious which side to block but there are some unfair exceptions in which some enemies and bosses' attacks are either so fast or their telegraphing is so similar to another attack that it's nearly impossible to differentiate while reacting to them.

All of the above considered, this results in a very slow and deliberate gameplay loop that quickly becomes exceedingly repetitive, stale, and bland, especially when you learn the visual cues of the regular enemies and have no trouble with them. Following that, it just becomes a wearying task of getting through the same levels and enemies just to get to the boss in order to learn their visual cues. Frankly, the game just doesn't respect your time.

The attacks themselves also look and feel flaccid and underwhelming: they don't look spectacular and don't feel like they have any weight to them, although this is probably due to the less than stellar animations that the game uses as well as a limitation of the 2D view. Furthermore, this is egregiously exacerbated later on when unarmored enemies take multiple hits to kill which makes you feel like you're wielding a Wiffle bat (a plastic baseball bat) rather than an actual bastard sword.

The game has two modes: a campaign mode and an endless mode. In the campaign mode, you progress through five levels and five bosses to finish the game and can choose to continue the file using a "New Game Plus" feature up to two more times. Each iteration of New Game Plus very slightly increases the enemies' reaction times and awards you with a modified title screen upon completion. Throughout each level, you encounter a variety of unique enemies but the game starts recycling enemy types during the last two levels and makes them stronger and faster. In the endless mode, your goal is to defeat as many enemies as possible without dying. After 10 kills, you proceed to the next level (looping after the fifth) and encounter certain enemies based on your kill count.

[h3]Graphics[/h3]
The graphics exclusively use pixel art but the character sprites don't look very good; however, this is more than likely due to the poor animations rather than the pixel art itself (although the main character looks particularly atrocious, especially their walking animation). That being said, the backgrounds look fantastic, are quite immersive, and are rife with little details to discover.

[h3]Sound[/h3]
The soundtrack is composed of surprisingly good medieval-style music that is fitting and serves as good background noise but is ultimately forgettable. Meanwhile, the sound effects are hit-or-miss: some are resounding and accurate while others are completely unsuitable and pitiful since they don't match what they would sound like in real life — the worst example being when you hit certain unarmored enemies with your bastard sword because it sounds more like a friendly "bop" rather than the slicing of flesh.

[h3]Story[/h3]
The story is distinctly minimalistic and is explained entirely through a still-image with no text after the completion of each of the five levels. What's more fascinating is that these still-images resemble propaganda posters which is especially interesting because it could mean that [spoiler]the main character is in fact the villain in this story[/spoiler] and I always think that this is an enthralling plot device when used correctly. Ultimately, it's very vague and left up to your interpretation but I think this is one of the few good points of the game.

[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
As far as the controls are concerned, keyboard users must use six separate buttons to attack and block and I found this awkward to get used to — I still pressed the wrong button every once in a while even after over four hours of playing on a keyboard. Controller users are less fortunate as their controls can't be changed at all and the existing ones are somehow even less intuitive by default because you are required to hold down a shoulder button and press one of the attack buttons to block.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
This game is honestly a chore and is actually quite similar to the quarter-munching arcade games from over 30 years ago. In fact, I think it would have fit right in and made a lot of money if it were released on an arcade machine back then but I don't think that this formula has aged very well in the intervening decades since arcades were popular.

Many other reviewers liken this game to Dark Souls and call this a 2D version of it but even Dark Souls is more forgiving than this game. Sadly, this game is borderline unfair if you don't have a good reaction speed and it ultimately doesn't respect your time since it requires you to needlessly grind out the same levels over and over just to have a chance at defeating the boss at the end of the level.

If this is your kind of game and this review has only solidified your opinion of it then you should consider waiting for it to go on sale for [u][url=https://steamdb.info/app/371550/]70% off 1.49 USD[/url][/u] which has historically been its average low. But consider yourself warned because I definitely regret purchasing it and inadvertently acquiring the first achievement three years ago as this eventually impelled me to 100% complete it.

No Pest Productions tarafından geliştirilen ve yayınlanan bu oyun, düşmanın saldırılarına ve savunmalarına sürekli uyum sağlamayı gerektiren derin bir oynanışa sahiptir.

Oyunun güçlü yönlerinden biri, düşman türlerindeki büyük çeşitliliktir. Fethedilecek 20'den fazla benzersiz düşmanla, oyuncular farklı saldırı düzenlerine ve zayıflıklara sahip çok sayıda düşmanla karşılaşacaklar. Oyuncular her bir düşmanı yenmek için yeni stratejiler keşfedebileceğinden, bu çeşitlilik oyunun tekrar değerine katkıda bulunur.

Oyunda, her biri kendi zorlukları ve düşmanları olan 5 seviye bulunmaktadır. Buna ek olarak, oyun, oyunu daha fazla zorlukla tekrar oynamak isteyen oyuncular için bir New Game Plus modu sunuyor. Ayrıca oyuncuların mümkün olduğunca çok sayıda düşmanı yenerek yüksek skorlar elde edebilecekleri bir Sonsuz Dövüşçü modu da bulunmaktadır.

A Bastard's Tale, oyuncuların oyun tarzlarına en uygun kontrolleri seçmelerine olanak tanıyan kontrolör ve klavye özelleştirmesini destekler. Genel olarak, bu oyun benzersiz bir oyun mekaniği ve zor bir düşmana karşı zafer kazanmanın getirdiği tatmin duygusundan hoşlanan oyunculara hitap edecek gerçek bir meydan okuma sunuyor.

[b][u]Overview:[/u][/b]
I should probably mention right off the bat that “frustration” games are not my thing. Anything that relies on cruel difficulty or archaic control schemes or cheap one-shots are beyond annoying in my mind. Usually I do my best to avoid them.

However, this game touted pure skill to play and dark souls-esque combat. Being a fan of that series, I decided to give this game a try, and low and behold… it’s not really a “frustration” game. It’s surprisingly fair, but it still does have several flaws which can turn off even a veteran player.

[b][u]The Fun:[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Excellent sound design
[*] Beautiful pixelated graphics
[*] Triumphant, yet foreboding orchestral direction
[/list]

[b][u]The Not-Fun:[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Required to read the controls before playing
[*] Confusing sprites for directional-based combat
[*] Strange and unalterable controls (on controller)
[/list]

[b][u]The Gist:[/u][/b]
Overall the game is fun and has a solid difficulty curve to it. However, the predominant issue that prevents me from recommending it is the sprite reading required. For most enemies it’s very easy to determine which direction their attack is coming in (and for some there are some creative tells, such as the crow enemy from the third level). However, there are a handful (such as the black knight and the bo master) where it’s extremely difficult to determine which way the attack is coming from. And because this sprite reading is extra difficult and the defending windows are very tight, there’s a lot of misread attacks which result in quick death.

If some of these sprites were to be tuned, I would gladly return and complete the game. But in its current state (which I fear will never be altered), I cannot recommend this game unless you’re patient enough to decipher the attacks through sheer trial and error.

Игра в неё первые 2 часа я не мог не заметить, как же сложно вовремя среагировать и не запутаться в постановке блока(это будет ваше первое и серьёзное препятствие). Но после прохождения 2-ух уровней вы сможете ловко и уверенно защищаться от простых ударов в 3 стороны, ведь дальше враги будут бить точно также с небольшими изменениями.
Достаточно разнообразные враги будут вам попадаться, лишь немного корректируя своё поведение в бою.

Gameplay: Дуэли 1VS1 с разными типами врагов. Нужно найти особый подход, чтобы убить враг. Я насчитал около 15 таких разнообразных врагов, также на каждом уровне где то на середине вам дадут флакон с хилкой.
Игра не даёт никакого обучения или советов. Я сам путём захода в настройки управления увидел, что могу уклоняться и то на какие кнопки жать, чтобы бить и ставить блок. Это минус.

Стоит также понять, что игра сложная. А на одном уровне больше половины из игроков просто сдались. Если не любите хардкор, стоит воздержаться от покупки. Ну или взять по скидке, чтобы жалко не было, что вы потратили на это деньги.
Здесь по мимо основной сюжетной игры есть режим выживания.
Рекомендую эту игру потому в нечто подобное могли не играть и получить новый игровой опыт, в меру хардкорно, классный и простой Gameplay.Даб-Даб

"A Bastard's Tale" is not for the easily angered or those who give up. This game has incredibly difficult mechanics, definitely, but that's the point. This title makes you master every individual encounter and every technique there is. This game is absolutely a rewarding experience. It has some good pixel art and designs. Anyone calling this game too hard, shoddy, a souls clone (this game has nothing in common with dark souls other than you control a knight) or poorly controlled are simply the faint of heart. If you are looking for a simple yet challenging retro experience, this is a good choice.
